name: Pan-Iranism
summary: Pan-Iranism is an Iranian nationalist current that calls for cultural, and in its stronger forms political, unity of the Iranian peoples, summed up in the slogan of the Iranian plateau under one flag. It arose in the 1920s to 1940s as a reaction to Pan-Turkism and Pan-Arabism, and is secular, hostile to Islam's role in Iranian identity, anti-communist and keen on pre-Islamic heritage and the Persian language. Its parties demanded recovery of lost lands such as Bahrain, the Caucasus and Afghanistan, though its present mainstream stresses cultural integration instead.
scope: The Iranian Pan-Iranist movement as it existed from the 1940s to the 1970s and in its present party form: Mahmoud Afshar's early formulation, the Pan-Iranist Party (Pezeshkpour) and the Nation of Iran Party (Forouhar). It excludes Pan-Iranism outside Iran (for example Tajik parties) and treats the radical irredentist stream as the historical core and the cultural-integration stance as the modern mainstream. Sources are mostly secondary and the party's own programme texts could not be read in full, so many economic and social answers are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Nationalisation and economic independence point to a statist outlook, so state-guaranteed health care is a plausible inference; the sources do not mention health policy.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from the party's anti-capitalist, nationalising economics; wage policy itself is not discussed in the sources.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Nation of Iran Party opposed capitalism and favoured nationalised industry and self-sufficiency, which leans against trusting free markets over the state.

public-ownership.rationale: The party advocated nationalisation of industries as part of economic independence, so public ownership of energy and utilities fits.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Anti-capitalist rhetoric suggests support, but no tax programme is documented.

unions-good.rationale: Anti-communist yet anti-capitalist; nothing documented on unions, and a nationalist party could go either way.

property-fundamental.rationale: Nationalisation of industry implies private property can be overridden for national interest; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Opposition to capitalism and foreign economic dependence implies tighter control of firms; inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: A statist, nationalist economic stance makes welfare cuts unlikely to be a priority; inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: The party's anti-communism and national-interest framing favour state or national ownership over worker collectives.

surveillance-ok.rationale: A security-minded nationalist party with paramilitary organisation would likely accept surveillance; not documented.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Disciplined, nationalist-conservative style suggests opposition; inferred, not documented.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The Nation of Iran Party's own organ expressed racial and anti-Semitic positions, and a nationalist party would resist speech limits.

strong-leader.rationale: Under Pezeshkpour the party had a ranked, uniformed paramilitary structure, suggesting comfort with strong leadership.

state-harmful.rationale: Nationalism that places all policy in the service of the nation's interests is statist; the state is the instrument of unity.

limit-guns.rationale: Members did not carry weapons even in the paramilitary phase; inferred preference for state monopoly of force.

empower-police-military.rationale: Uniformed ranks and a nationalist, territorial-recovery agenda favour a strong army and security apparatus.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Nationalist-conservative orientation suggests opposition; no documented stance.

decide-locally.rationale: The movement exists to unify Iranian peoples under one state, so devolution away from the national centre runs against it.

rehabilitation.rationale: Nothing in the sources on criminal justice; adherents have no distinct view.

traditional-family.rationale: Right-wing, nationalist classification suggests support for traditional family; inferred.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Right-wing nationalist label and period make support unlikely; inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from nationalist, conservative orientation; no documented stance.

more-religion-public.rationale: The party is defined today largely by opposition to Islam's influence on Iranian culture and lists state secularism as an ideal.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Racialised nationalism and focus on Iranian unity make remedial racial programmes an unlikely cause; inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; a nationalist party would be unlikely to adopt this view.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The party emphasised reviving pre-Islamic Iranian values, preserving the Persian language and promoting Iranian heritage, which this statement restates.

gradual-change.rationale: The party sought a break from foreign dependence and recovery of lost land, which sits uneasily with incrementalism; inferred.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Nationalist emphasis on a unified Iranian nation implies restricting non-Iranian inflows; not documented.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The party's symbol stands against unequal relations with major powers and for sovereignty, implying scepticism of supranational authority.

free-trade.rationale: Economic independence and self-sufficiency are stated goals, which cut against open trade.

nation-first.rationale: The party held that all policy should serve national interests, which is this statement.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Sovereignty-minded and anti-great-power; would suspect such interventions; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: A nationalist movement built on a bounded Iranian nation rejects open borders; contrary to its core.

limit-growth.rationale: Economic development and independence are priorities; no environmental stance documented.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The sources show no environmental policy at all, and nothing in nationalist or economic-independence principles points either way, so this is a neutral placeholder.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Pahlavi-era modernising nationalism was pro-technology; inferred for a movement of that milieu.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Sovereignty and independence themes suggest support for national nuclear capacity; inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: Split: the Forouhar wing opposed the Pahlavi system, while the Pezeshkpour wing worked within it.

experts-over-public.rationale: Nothing in the documented programme addresses technocracy versus popular input, and the movement mixed parliamentary politics with elite-led nationalism, so no direction can be inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Nationalisation and self-sufficiency lean toward planning but the party was also anti-communist; no clear view.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not discussed; its nationalisation favours public ownership but nothing on market socialism.

land-value-tax.rationale: Fiscal design was never part of the party's documented goals, which centred on unity, territory and economic independence.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance taxation does not appear in any source on the party; its nationalising stance gives only a faint lean, not enough for a position.

basic-income.rationale: An anachronistic policy idea that Pan-Iranists of the 1940s to 1970s never discussed, and nothing in their principles settles it.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic independence, self-sufficiency and ending foreign dependence imply protecting domestic industry.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Nationalisation of industries and economic independence imply state direction of strategic sectors.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The party's economics were about nationalisation and independence, not the distribution of property among small owners versus firms, so adherents have no distinct view.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The party was anti-communist and anti-Marxist; abolishing money and wages is a communist aim it rejected.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A statist national-economic outlook makes abolition unlikely; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not documented; nationalism could suit corporatism but the party also took democratic positions.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Nation of Iran Party favoured a secular democracy, and the Pan-Iranist Party competed as an opposition party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Split: the Pezeshkpour faction worked inside the Pahlavi system while the Forouhar faction was anti-monarchist.

democracy-best.rationale: The Nation of Iran Party favoured secular democracy and later Pan-Iranist leaders say they support pluralism, but earlier phases had paramilitary features.

direct-votes.rationale: Referendum-style lawmaking is not documented for the party; it contested parliamentary seats but proposed no direct-democracy mechanism.

workers-councils.rationale: Council power is a communist-left idea; the party was anti-communist and national rather than class-based.

right-to-secede.rationale: The ideology exists to preserve and extend Iranian territorial unity, and it began as a reaction to Pan-Turkist threats to territorial integrity.

natural-rulers.rationale: Racial and Aryanist elements in the party's thinking suggest hierarchy, but this is not stated as a doctrine.

political-violence-never.rationale: The party clashed with Tudeh supporters in the streets and had a paramilitary structure, so it did not hold pacifism.

war-builds-character.rationale: Paramilitary style hints at martial values but nothing documented.

separate-church-state.rationale: State secularism is listed as part of the party's ideology and it opposes Islam's influence on culture.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The party opposes the post-1979 Islamic government and religious influence on Iranian culture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A nationalist-statist movement concerned with territory and security would reject privatised defence.

military-superiority.rationale: Recovery of lost territories implied military strength, though the source calls these goals impractical.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The unity sought is among Iranian peoples sharing heritage, with some racial thinking; yet it embraces several Iranian ethnic groups, so only moderate.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nationalism makes the nation, not class, the historical agent, and the party was anti-communist.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Anti-capitalist but nationalist; equality of outcome is not a stated goal.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Centralised nationalism would not endorse group authority over land; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The party denounced British rule in Bahrain and great-power dominance, so some redress is plausible, but reparations are not documented.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-Iranism is defined as a call for socio-cultural unity among all Iranian peoples, and its slogan puts the Iranian plateau under one flag.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The nationalist ethos stresses duty to the nation, yet no source takes a stand on individual self-interest as morally good, so the answer is left neutral.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Policy must serve national interests and the party used a disciplined paramilitary form, favouring duty to the community.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental ethics lie outside the sources on this movement; no position can be inferred from its principles.

limit-population.rationale: Demographic policy is not discussed in the sources, and a nationalist wish for a strong nation pulls in opposite directions from development concerns.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: A modernising nationalism that sought national strength and economic independence would treat industrial civilisation as a source of power, not a disaster; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The party wanted national development and independence but never addressed institutional disruption by technology, so this is left neutral.

human-enhancement.rationale: A question from a much later era that the movement never faced; its principles do not decide it.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; nationalists would not hand decisions to algorithms; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Never addressed; a security-minded, statist nationalism would likely favour state access, but this is only an inference.

restore-past-order.rationale: The party sought to revive pre-Islamic values and ancient glory, though as part of a modern nation project.

results-over-ideology.rationale: A committed ideological movement; not pragmatic by self-description.

direct-action.rationale: The Pezeshkpour wing contested parliamentary seats, and both wings were parties.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources do not describe any view on whether methods must prefigure goals; the party used both street clashes and parliament, so no pattern emerges.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A communist-utopian idea contrary to the party's anti-communism; inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution by need is a communist formula, and the party defined itself against communism and clashed with Tudeh supporters.

production-for-use.rationale: Anti-capitalist but anti-communist; this is a Marxist phrasing it did not adopt.

profit-exploitation.rationale: A Marxist claim; the party was anti-communist while opposing capitalism on national grounds.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Direct communist doctrine, opposed by the party, which fought Tudeh supporters.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivised agriculture is a communist programme; the party's anti-communism makes opposition the likely answer, though farming policy itself is not documented.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Anti-capitalist but not in Leninist terms; nothing documented.

taxation-theft.rationale: A nationalising, state-centred economic programme depends on taxation and treats the state as the agent of the nation, so calling tax theft is contrary to it.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberal limits on state power are not discussed; a nationalist party with a paramilitary phase and a later turn to pluralism gives no clear lean.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Nationalism treats the nation as a unit with collective claims.

conscription.rationale: Military-style discipline and territorial ambitions imply support for conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism privileges belonging to the state.

state-as-business.rationale: Treating citizens as customers of a state that can be exited conflicts with a nation-bound, anti-capitalist outlook, though this is inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses the concept of freedom as material capacity, so the answer is neutral.

media-academia-power.rationale: The party itself began among Tehran University students, but there is no documented claim that media and universities rule over elected officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The party's organ expressed racial positions, though they are not documented as a genetic claim about ability.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation through families and trade bodies is not documented for this movement, which competed as a parliamentary party.

total-state.rationale: The paramilitary form hints at authoritarianism but its later leaders embraced pluralism.

national-rebirth.rationale: Reviving pre-Islamic values and recovering lost lands expresses a rebirth of a once-great nation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The radical stream seeks to unite Iranian-inhabited lands and revive Achaemenid-like boundaries, while the modern mainstream favours cultural integration only.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: A modern nationalist party built on the nation-state and parliament would find feudal personal oaths foreign; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Feudal bondage is incompatible with a modernising national movement; inferred.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed; unlikely given Enlightenment-style nationalism.

universal-morality.rationale: The sources record no view on moral universalism; the movement's cultural particularism may lean against it, but not clearly enough to score.

single-common-good.rationale: Policy serves one national interest, rather than balancing group interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The Nation of Iran Party is described as anti-Semitic, though the mainstream Pan-Iranist stance on Israel is not documented.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Union of Iranian peoples beyond borders implies welcoming Iranian kin; inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: The party stressed preserving and promoting Persian, though Persian never fell out of use, so this is inferred sympathy.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democratic control of firms by workers belongs to the left and sits against the party's national-interest framing; inferred opposition.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance mechanisms are not discussed in any source on the movement.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Macroeconomic fiscal rules are not documented for the party; its economic content was independence and nationalisation.

economic-freedom.rationale: The party favoured state-led independence and nationalisation, so it would not tie political freedom to economic freedom in the liberal sense.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rule by moral exemplars is not documented for this movement, which operated through parties and parliament.

national-self-determination.rationale: Split inside the doctrine: it claims national unity for Iranians but rejected recognition of Azerbaijan SSR and Pakistan.

force-without-un.rationale: Aimed to recover territory, which the party accepted would depend on its own initiative; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Secularism and opposition to Islam's influence imply an anti-clerical rationalism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Nationalism puts citizens first, but welfare was not part of the documented programme, so this is an inference at low confidence.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditionality is not addressed by the sources; no lean can be derived from nationalist or anti-capitalist themes.

class-collaboration.rationale: The party placed national interest above class and opposed communism, implying class cooperation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Preserving Iranian heritage and reviving pre-Islamic culture was central to the party, so sacrificing heritage institutions for novelty is opposed.

dominated-front.rationale: The party's symbol protests unequal relations with major powers and it fought British control of Bahrain.

workers-nation.rationale: Nationalist and anti-communist, it opposes internationalist class organisation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Pahlavi-era secular nationalism backed women's public role; this party's stance is not documented.

ban-interest.rationale: A secular, anti-Islamist party would not adopt a religious ban.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Racial thought existed but segregation law is not documented, and its goal is unity among Iranian peoples.

state-class-instrument.rationale: This is the Marxist theory of the state, which the party opposed; it treated the state as the nation's instrument.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Strong support for Mossadegh's oil nationalisation implies valuing oil output under national control.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Persianisation of minorities was the nationalist norm of the era; the party stresses cultural integration.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not documented; a modern conspiracy theory of a later period.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral system design is not documented for the party; a small party might favour it, but that is not stated.

national-mission.rationale: Aims are unity and recovery, not exporting a political system.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Feminist structural analysis does not appear in the sources and is unlikely in a nationalist party of the era; inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The party was an opposition party with outsider rhetoric; not detailed.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Racial thinking existed but eugenic policy is not documented.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Accountability for past security force abuses is not discussed; the movement sat in parliament under the Shah and gave no recorded view.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Nationalised industry and a state-led nationalist project reject a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Some racial thought exists in the movement but is not documented on this point, and unity extends across Iranian groups.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Citizens' equality is plausible, but racialised nationalism complicates a flat answer.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The party was not socialist, so the debate on building socialism in one country was not its own.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Whether settler states are colonial projects is not covered by any source on Pan-Iranism.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Reza Shah's secular nationalism replaced religious courts with uniform law; the party shares the secular outlook.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Secular and critical of Islamic influence, so it would not favour such restrictions; inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A Hindu-nationalist demand with no place in Iranian secular nationalism; inferred opposition.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: State secularism is a listed element of the party's ideology, so religious instruction in state schools would be opposed.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This is a Marxist-Leninist argument about the socialist state; the party was not socialist and gave no view.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Secular democracy was the Nation of Iran Party's declared aim.

trade-surplus.rationale: Economic independence and self-sufficiency imply a mercantile emphasis.

population-transfer.rationale: The movement's declared aim is cultural integration of Iranian peoples, not expelling minorities; the source on its territorial plans does not document transfers.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Territorial recovery claims and a paramilitary tradition run directly against this absolute rule.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Racial and nationalist outlook tends to see peoples in competition; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The party itself is banned and criticises that, but a nationalist party might still support banning communists.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican political theory is not part of the movement's documented thought, so no position is inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: The Pezeshkpour wing sat in the Majlis and later leaders endorse pluralism and democracy, which implies acceptance of checks and balances.

vanguard-party.rationale: The need for a revolutionary vanguard is a Leninist doctrine; the party was anti-communist and national rather than class-based.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The programme emphasises national unity and independence rather than class-based claims, so no clear stance on prioritising the poor is documented.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy that has no counterpart in the documented programme.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: National unity and class cooperation over class conflict suggest sympathy for limiting strikes; not stated directly.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Malthusian explanations of poverty are not discussed in the sources.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: National-unity ideology plus racial thinking suggests this; not documented.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Selection by lottery is alien to a nationalist, party-based movement that contested elections; inferred opposition.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The party's paramilitary roots suggest some tolerance for emergency measures, but its later turn to pluralism and its own experience of being banned pull the other way.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Statist, nationalising economics make price controls plausible, though this is not documented.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Nation of Iran Party sought a secular democracy and the Pan-Iranist Party later cooperated with other opposition groups, so state control of media is unlikely; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: A party-commanded army is a one-party-state device; the movement operated as a party within a parliamentary or opposition setting.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: A bounded Iranian nation of shared heritage implies a cautious approach to citizenship; not documented directly.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Capping officials' pay is a left-populist measure not documented for this movement.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Under Pezeshkpour the party had ranks, uniforms and a paramilitary structure, consistent with binding discipline; later leaders softened this.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Sovereignty-focused; its symbol protests great-power inequality.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Constitutional allocation of command powers is not addressed in the sources.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Episcopal church government is a Christian question with no counterpart in the Iranian movement.

clerical-rule.rationale: It opposes the Islamic Republic and clerical influence on culture.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A strongly nationalist movement that put national interest above all would reject working for its own government's defeat.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The party held a secular, anti-clerical outlook, which makes moral censorship of art unlikely, though censorship itself is not documented.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The Nation of Iran Party's goal was a secular democracy, which suggests accepting term limits; no source states a view.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall elections are not mentioned in any source on the movement.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The crossed-out equal sign symbolises refusal of unequal relations with major powers.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Abolishing rental housing is a radical egalitarian measure that does not appear in the programme; inferred opposition.

people-in-arms.rationale: Paramilitary but disciplined ranks, with no weapons carried.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The movement is urban, university-born and modernising, and gives no sign of romanticising rural life; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The party sought to unite Iran's ethnic groups and recover Caucasus, Bahrain and Afghanistan; the modern version stresses cultural unity.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The party was founded at Tehran University and drew intellectuals and students, so it would not accept this charge.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Aryanist, Persian-centred nationalism ranks Iranian civilisation highly.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment is not discussed in the sources; a nationalist, conservative-leaning party would likely accept it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Sex education is not addressed by the sources; secular modernising tendencies and conservative tendencies cancel out.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: A secular party hostile to religious influence on culture would oppose teaching creationism in public schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed in any source; the movement's mix of secular and conservative traits gives no direction.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The ideology defines unity by shared Iranian ancestry across borders, which fits descent-based citizenship; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Pahlavi nationalism, whose milieu the party shared, banned or marginalised non-Persian languages.

religious-exemptions.rationale: A uniform secular legal order, as under Reza Shah, leaves little room for religious exemptions from general laws; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: A nationalist movement stressing cultural unity would not prize non-conformity; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Opposition to foreign economic dependence suggests sympathy for cancelling poor-country debt, though the party never addressed debt.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The party tied independence to nationalising industry and ending foreign dependence.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The sources do not say how Pan-Iranists would rewrite a constitution, so this is left neutral.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The party's strong development and independence goals might justify limits, yet it also endorsed democracy; no clear lean.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Aid obligations are not addressed; nationalist priorities cut against, and anti-imperial resentment of rich powers cuts for, so neutral.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Sovereignty and independence from major powers are central, so national nuclear weapons would fit; the era predates the question, so this is inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The question matters little to a movement split between accommodation with the monarchy and republicanism.

central-bank-independence.rationale: A statist, nationalising economic outlook disfavours insulating monetary policy from elected government; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The party denounced Iran's acceptance of Bahrain's independence in 1971.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Nationalisation of industry for the national interest implies property is justified by service to the nation.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The party was anti-communist but this Marxist-internal debate is not its own.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is not part of the documented programme.

collective-defense.rationale: Not documented; anti-alliance leaning countered by common security.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Its demand for Bahrain and rejection of Azerbaijan SSR reflects such logic, though consent of the people is not its test.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Anti-clericalism and secularism are listed ideological elements.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The Pezeshkpour wing worked within the Pahlavi system while the Forouhar wing opposed monarchy, so adherents are split.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The movement began as a defence of territorial integrity against separatism.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Unity and uniform integration of Iranian lands is the goal, so asymmetric autonomy within a larger state does not fit; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Pre-Islamic glorification but the Nation of Iran Party was anti-monarchist; sacral kingship is not documented.

flat-income-tax.rationale: A statist, anti-capitalist economic outlook would not favour a flat tax; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: The movement included racial thinking that treats traits as innate, so a purely environmental account is unlikely; low confidence.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is unaddressed in the sources and no principle of the movement bears on it, so adherents have no distinct view.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The movement operated in a constitutional framework and the Nation of Iran Party favoured democracy, so an unbound ruler is unlikely.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not discussed in the sources.

leader-cult.rationale: The Pezeshkpour wing worked within the monarchy, but no documented cult.

equal-parenting.rationale: Child custody law is unaddressed in the sources, and neither nationalism nor economic independence bears on it.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist internal question; the party's anti-communism puts it against the premise.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land reform was not part of the party's documented programme, and nationalism does not clearly point either way.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return is not addressed; the party's territorial claims are not framed in terms of displaced people.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Radical Pan-Iranism claims Iranian-inhabited lands in the Caucasus, Central Asia and elsewhere on the basis of the Iranian peoples living there.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The party opposes Islamic law and Islam's influence on Iranian culture, so punishing apostasy runs directly against it.

women-must-cover.rationale: Reza Shah's secular nationalism discouraged veiling and the party opposes Islamist rule, so legally required covering is rejected.

common-currency.rationale: The movement stresses sovereignty and independence from outside powers, which cuts against ceding a national currency; inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-Iranism is the call for unity among peoples of shared Iranian ancestry and culture across existing borders, as its slogan on one flag says.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Persian-centred nationalism with integration, not minority self-governance.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's own aim is unity of kin peoples across borders rather than minority strategy elsewhere.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Nationalist idealism treats the nation and culture as drivers; Marxism rejected.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust policy is not documented, and its nationalising bent gives no clear direction.

no-bailouts.rationale: Rescue of failing banks is unaddressed; statist leanings and anti-capitalist rhetoric pull in opposite directions, so neutral.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Judicial review versus majority rule is not documented for Pan-Iranism.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas are not addressed and sit poorly with a nationalist, conservative-leaning outlook; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Self-sufficiency and an end to foreign dependence were stated goals, though a closed bloc with colonies is not part of the programme; low confidence.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Labour and environmental clauses in trade agreements are not addressed; the movement is more concerned with independence than standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: Replacing material incentives with moral ones is a communist theme not documented here.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Members did not carry weapons; foco theory is a Marxist idea.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The wings split, with the Nation of Iran Party anti-monarchist and the Pezeshkpour wing working within the Pahlavi monarchy.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The movement is built around Iranian civilisation and pre-Islamic heritage, so teaching history centred on it fits its core.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The movement is anti-imperial and sovereignty-minded, and the party protested great-power dominance, so rule by a more advanced society is opposed.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nationalism builds pride via schooling, as Reza Shah's state did.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Racial preferences in admissions are not addressed; a nationalist wing without remedial-racial aims would likely oppose them.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform of this kind is not discussed in the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The party opposed capitalism on national grounds but did not rely on a Marxist crisis theory, so no clear view is documented.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Radical streams aim to revive the Achaemenid boundaries and influence.

delink-world-market.rationale: Self-sufficiency and an end to foreign dependence were stated goals, which resemble delinking; held at low confidence since the sources do not mention it.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This is a Marxist-Leninist thesis about imperialism that the party did not discuss.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: A state-centred nationalist movement would not endorse unrestricted private discrimination; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional design for rights protection is not covered in the sources.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Pan-Iranists regard Russian-imposed treaties of 1813 and 1828 and British Bahrain arrangements as illegitimate losses of Iranian land.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Pezeshkpour wing worked within the monarchy while the Forouhar wing was anti-monarchist, so adherents split on rulers being chosen by election.

minority-veto.rationale: A veto for dissenting minorities is incompatible with a movement built on national unity and territorial integrity.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The party opposed the post-1979 government and had a faction that opposed the Pahlavi system, but no doctrine of lawful resistance is documented.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The party sat in the Majlis and was a semi-opposition party in parliament, implying a constitutionalist outlook.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is outside the documented concerns of the movement, so no position follows from its principles.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use for food and research is outside the documented concerns of the movement, so no position follows.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: No source records an elite-duty ethic for this movement, so adherents have no distinct view.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement is an activist political party that urges engagement for the national cause, which contradicts a withdrawal ideal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Frankfurt-school critique of media is not part of the movement.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian thesis that does not feature in the sources on Pan-Iranism.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Opposition to foreign economic domination suggests agreement with the broad claim that rich powers extract from poorer ones, but this is inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Nationalism reserves public life to full members of the nation; not stated explicitly in the sources.

party-own-road.rationale: The party was not a communist party, so the question of independence from another country's party does not apply.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Economic independence and ending dependence on foreign powers.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The key demand was the recovery of Bahrain, plus the Caucasus and Afghanistan.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed, and an Iranian-unity movement would not frame politics as descendants of pre-colonial peoples over settlers.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Critics describe Pan-Iranism as having been a fascist current, and adherents would not endorse the label's opposite as a founding value.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The party was anti-communist, but its own critics label it fascist and no source records its stance on equating the two.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American historical dispute not addressed by Pan-Iranism.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: A movement that prizes heritage and symbols of the nation would lean toward keeping historic monuments; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender-policy debates of this kind postdate and are outside the movement's documented concerns.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is outside the movement's documented concerns, so no position is inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Iranian civilisational distinctiveness is a theme, so adherents would accept that political forms may suit a civilisation; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The party worked within the Pahlavi order and has no documented doctrine of the army as political guardian.

paid-care-work.rationale: Recognition of unpaid care labour is outside the movement's documented concerns, so no position follows.

filial-duty.rationale: Traditional family values are an inference from the party's conservative-nationalist classification.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not documented; the movement was a party-political one that did not advance exam-based appointment.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic independence and an end to foreign dependence were stated goals, which supports blocking foreign purchase of strategic firms.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Family law is outside the documented concerns of the movement; its secular and conservative traits point opposite ways.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandate is a council-communist idea not found in the sources.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Private pension accounts conflict with a statist, nationalising economic outlook; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land held only by use is a radical agrarian idea not found in the programme, and nationalisation was aimed at industry.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The party sat in parliament and endorsed constitutional politics, so parliamentary approval of budgets would be accepted.

single-official-language.rationale: Persian-centred nationalism and the party's emphasis on preserving Persian.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Economic independence and nationalism make restrictions on foreign ownership likely; not stated.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Outcome-based discrimination doctrine is not addressed by the sources.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumer culture is not discussed in sources on the movement, and nothing in its principles settles it.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The movement backed ethnically related groups abroad, such as Kurds and Tajiks, in rhetoric, but arming insurgents is not documented.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Cold War bloc discipline is not addressed; the party opposed communism but gave no view on great powers invading allies.

corporate-influence.rationale: Anti-capitalist and anti-foreign-dependence positions suggest agreement that corporations hold too much sway; inferred.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Sovereignty concerns imply support for restricting foreign funding; not documented.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: A nationalist strong-nation outlook suggests favouring natural population growth; not stated.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local residency rules on property are not addressed, though nationalism favours restrictions on outsiders to a limited degree.

job-guarantee.rationale: Statist leanings give only a weak lean toward a job guarantee and the sources are silent, so neutral.

democratic-peace.rationale: The movement's irredentist ambitions and non-democratic phases make it indifferent to this liberal thesis.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Nationalists stress duty to the state, so a denial of general obligation to obey law is unlikely; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Sovereignty is central, and the party protested great-power interference, which supports a rule against intervention; not stated as an absolute.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not addressed by sources on the movement, so no view is inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Anti-Semitism and anti-Bahai are listed elements in Nation of Iran Party, the strand of the party.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: A radical anti-institution demand incompatible with a conservative-nationalist outlook; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom-of-information law is not addressed and nothing in nationalist principles settles it.

local-production.rationale: Economic self-sufficiency could imply a preference for national production, but localism as such is not documented.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement was an organised party with ranks and structure, so small informal networks without parties are rejected.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Sovereignty is central, and the party protested unequal relations with major powers, which supports national constitutional primacy.

religious-nation.rationale: The party opposes Islam's influence on Iranian identity and instead defines the nation by shared Iranian heritage and language.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The party's crossed-out equals sign condemns unequal relations with major powers and calls for protecting sovereignty.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Unity and central integration of Iranian lands cut against regions keeping their own revenue; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Communist property arrangement not addressed; the party opposed communism but did not discuss personal possessions.

defeat-communism.rationale: The party was anti-communist and clashed with Tudeh supporters in Tehran, so coexistence was not its line.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Models for delivering public services are not discussed in the sources on this movement.

religion-illusion.rationale: The party is secular and hostile to Islam's cultural influence, but no source records that it called religion an illusion, so adherents are split.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The party was anti-capitalist on national grounds and would not credit capitalism as progressive; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed, and an anti-communist nationalist movement would not usually frame equality this way; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Public provision of housework and childcare is a socialist-feminist demand not found in the sources.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Preserving the Persian language was a stated aim, and language purism was common in Iranian nationalism of the period; purging foreign words is inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not addressed by the sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small cooperative communes are a utopian-left idea that contradicts the party's national-state focus.

majority-settlement.rationale: Persianisation of minorities was the norm in Pahlavi nationalism, which the party shared; settlement policy itself is not documented.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The party was both anti-capitalist and anti-communist, which describes a third course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Claims on Bahrain, Caucasus, Afghanistan from historic Iranian rule.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The sources do not document denial, though the Nation of Iran Party organ expressed anti-Semitic positions; mainstream adherents are unlikely to adopt denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Sexual law is not addressed; the party's secular outlook argues against religion-based criminalisation while conservatism argues for it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The party itself was banned and works for democracy and cooperation with other opposition groups, so suppression of opposition is unlikely to be its stance.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The party is secular and opposes religious influence over the state, so blasphemy laws are rejected.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The movement protested British control of Bahrain and great-power dominance, so exploitation of dependencies is opposed.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The party opposes the pan-Islamism of the post-1979 government and would not accept a religious duty framing.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Removal of rulers who ignore religious law is an Islamist doctrine that the party's secularism rejects.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Direct participation in workplaces and universities is a New Left theme not found in the sources.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectional analysis is not addressed and unlikely in a nationalist movement; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; a conservative-nationalist movement is unlikely to support it.

assisted-dying.rationale: Medical ethics is not addressed, and secular and conservative tendencies cancel out.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Rejection of capitalism and communism together suggests a third-position view that transcends left and right.

alienated-labor.rationale: Alienation is a Marxist concept; the party defined itself against communism and rejected the framing.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The party opposes Islam's influence on Iranian culture, but nothing in the sources addresses Islam in Western countries.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The party is secular and rests authority on the nation, so divine origin of authority is rejected.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Secularism is a listed element of the party's ideology, supporting limits on religious dress in state institutions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Employment law on harassment is not addressed by the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: The party's economic programme was nationalist and statist; a social market synthesis is not documented either way.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: A movement with territorial recovery aims and a paramilitary phase would not favour abolishing armed forces.

rich-first.rationale: Unbalanced-growth strategies are not discussed in the sources, so adherents have no distinct view.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The party's symbol rejects unequal relations with major powers, which fits neutrality, though its Cold War anti-communism complicates this.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The wings split, with one working inside the Pahlavi monarchy and the other anti-monarchist.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: User-owned credit banks are not addressed, and the party's statist economics would favour state, not mutual, institutions; low confidence.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Opposition to foreign economic dependence suggests refusing conditions from international lenders; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: The Nation of Iran Party favoured secular democracy, which implies broad franchise.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist theory is not addressed and is unlikely in this movement.

reification.rationale: A Marxist theory of commodity relations that the party, being anti-communist and nationalist, did not adopt.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Not addressed; a critique of wealth ownership of the press is not documented.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The party operated within constitutional politics and sought democracy, supporting rule through public laws; not stated directly.

racial-franchise.rationale: Racial thinking existed in the Nation of Iran Party organ, but restricting the vote to one race is not documented and conflicts with its stated goal of democracy.

online-participation.rationale: Digital deliberation postdates the movement's documented phases, and no principle settles the question.

open-government-data.rationale: Open data governance postdates the movement's documented phases, and no principle settles the question.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The party's secularism and uniform law outlook argue against religion-based marriage restrictions; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The Nation of Iran Party organ expressed anti-Semitic positions, but no boycott campaign is documented, so adherents are not clearly in favour.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition assemblies are not addressed in the sources, and no principle of the movement settles it.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The movement is hostile to Islam's cultural role rather than interested in reforming it, so there is no documented stance on reinterpretation.

missingStatements.text: A nation's territory should include all the lands where its people and their cultural heritage have historically been found.
missingStatements.rationale: Radical Pan-Iranism seeks to unite Iranian-inhabited lands and revive historic boundaries, and the party's slogan puts the whole plateau under one flag.

missingStatements.text: A country should strengthen its identity by reviving the language and culture of its pre-religious ancient past.
missingStatements.rationale: The party emphasised reviving pre-Islamic Iranian values and heritage and preserving Persian.

notes: Strands differ: the Pezeshkpour wing worked inside the Pahlavi system and the Forouhar wing opposed it and formed the Nation of Iran Party; the modern party disclaims irredentism and favours plural democracy. The Nation of Iran Party organ expressed racial and anti-Semitic positions, which are a documented flaw rather than the movement's whole doctrine, so related answers are low confidence. Sources opened for this audit include no full primary programme text; Encyclopaedia Iranica was not accessible.
